verdict.rationale: Bento's 'signals' let you describe a failure mode in plain English; Bento then trains a detector on your traces, fires it in real time, and backfills history. Each signal has an editable prompt and config via the CLI, and releases are 'scored' against production history. That amounts to configurable, natural-language evaluators run over outputs, but the docs never call this LLM-as-a-judge and say it 'trains' a detector, so the judging mechanism is unclear. missing for 10: explicit LLM-as-a-judge evaluator documentation, choice of judge model and scoring rubrics/scales, per-output score semantics, independent or hands-on corroboration.
